notes: Unleash Open Source (unleashorg/unleash-server). On the first start, with an empty database, it creates the administrator from UNLEASH_DEFAULT_ADMIN_USERNAME (admin) and UNLEASH_DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD (a generated password shown on the first-run card), instead of the documented default admin / unleash4all. Both variables are read only while there are no users, so later changes do nothing: change the password in the web interface (Profile).
LOG_LEVEL is warn, as in the official compose file: Unleash writes the initial admin password into its info log line when it creates the account, and warn keeps it out of the container log.

PostgreSQL 17.11 (the docs accept 15 or newer) runs in its own container with its own named volume and no published port; database migrations run on every start of the Unleash container. DATABASE_SSL is off because the database is only reachable on the app's private network.

UNLEASH_URL is the site's address (used in links and invitation emails) and follows the domain. SECURE_HEADERS turns on Unleash's security headers and marks the session cookie Secure; the panel's HTTPS proxy sends X-Forwarded-Proto, which Unleash trusts. SEND_TELEMETRY is off.

No API tokens are created for you (the official compose file's insecure demo tokens are deliberately left out). Create a backend token for your server-side SDKs, or a frontend token for browsers, in Admin settings > API access, and use it as the Authorization header against https://<your domain>/api/client/features.
Outgoing email (invitations, password resets) needs SMTP settings (EMAIL_HOST and related variables); without them, add users with a password or share the reset link the admin interface shows.
The memory floor is 512m: Unleash sat at 76 to 95 MiB idle and peaked at 111 MiB (15 to 22 % of the limit), PostgreSQL at 35 to 44 MiB, on Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04.

Verified live on Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (RC-38): created from the 1-Click Recipes tab, Running in 48 s, sign-in as admin with the generated password (admin / unleash4all refused), a feature flag created and enabled in development, a backend API token created in the UI and GET /api/client/features listing the flag as enabled with that token, security headers and a Secure session cookie with no CSP errors, no admin password in the log, and a restart; every image ref below is in its tested list.
